narrative.overview:
TaskMate should feel like opening a well-kept paper daybook: warm, composed, and immediately useful. Soft neutral grounds create the atmosphere, crisp paper surfaces organize the content, and a single rust-red voice identifies action and completion. The result is professional without becoming corporate and personal without becoming decorative.

The system is restrained but not sterile. Newsreader gives major headings an editorial, human cadence; Aptos keeps instructions, task data, and release facts direct. A lightly offset paper layer and selective, broad shadows supply the only expressive depth, while clearly labeled, credible task content keeps the interface grounded in the product.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-neutral paper atmosphere with clean, legible contrast.
One rust-red action voice for downloads, checks, priorities, and focus.
Editorial display type paired with practical system sans-serif text.
Restrained depth built from tonal layers, offset paper, and broad soft shadows.
Direct copy and credible product proof instead of promotional ornament.

rules.name: The Rust Is an Action Rule
rules.body: Rust identifies a decision, state, or completion; it is never used as broad decorative fill.

rules.name: The Warm White Rule
rules.body: The canvas remains warm and white is reserved for the clearest raised surface, so hierarchy is visible before any shadow appears.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Newsreader speaks at display and proof-title scale; Aptos carries actions, instructions, metadata, and every scannable fact.

rules.name: The Short Promise Rule
rules.body: Display copy stays compact enough to preserve its deliberate line breaks and low line-height.

rules.name: The Proof Beside Promise Rule
rules.body: On wide screens, the product claim and credible task-list proof share the opening composition; on narrow screens, preserve the same reading order without squeezing either one.

rules.name: The Paper Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Establish hierarchy with surface tone and dividers first; reserve shadows for the action and the two proof-bearing cards.

rules.name: The One Expressive Tilt Rule
rules.body: Only the desktop task-list proof uses rotation and offset paper; remove its rotation on compact layouts so the content stays stable and readable.

rules.name: The Capsule Means Status Rule
rules.body: Full pills are reserved for progress and priority metadata, never for large calls to action or general containers.

dos: Do keep warm ground visible around clean paper surfaces.
Do reserve rust-red for action, completion, priority, and focus-related feedback.
Do pair direct claims with credible task or release details.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus and the reduced-motion override.
Do let dividers and spacing organize dense facts before adding elevation.
donts: Don't introduce gradients, glass panels, glows, abstract SaaS illustration, or decorative analytics.
Don't turn the rust accent into a large background field or a second typography color.
Don't make major actions pill-shaped; capsules belong to compact status.
Don't add competing card grids where a plain row or factual line is clearer.
Don't retain tilt or hover movement when the visitor requests reduced motion.
